## The short version

**Yes, there is an open door right now, and it is worse than "someone opens my app".** The key that protects the Servex endpoint is sitting in your **public** GitHub repo. Anyone who finds it can run any command on this PC.

I changed nothing, as you asked. The one thing I'd do before any proposal is rotate that key.

## The serious one: the Servex key is public

- **The repo is public.** GitHub's API reports `lew42/monorepo` as `"private": false`.
- **The key is in four committed files**, on `main` and `compliance/dev`. I fetched one from raw.githubusercontent.com with no login and the key was in it.
- **How it got there:** the connector URL (`.../mcp/remote/<key>`) was pasted into a chat, the chat was logged into `public/framework/ai/sessions/`, and the log sweep pushed it. The files:
  - `sessions/2026/10/13/session-730e8a7b/digest.json`
  - `sessions/2026/10/13/session-730e8a7b/prompt-audit.jsonl`
  - `sessions/2026/10/13/session-730e8a7b/mastermind-repo-slim/essence.jsonl`
  - `sessions/2026/11/06/spawned/mastermind-live-page/session.jsonl`
- **The key still works.** It has not changed since 2026-10-14. I tested it against the local gateway only (nothing left the PC): 107 tools, including `shell`, `write_file`, `edit_file` and `spawn_agent`.
- **The address is fixed and guessable:** `servex.lew42.com/mcp/remote/<key>`.
- **The same key is also the `monorepo.lew42.com` site key**, so it unlocks the site too.
- **Not leaked:** the Cloudflare API token is not in the repo or its history. The deployed static site (`lew42.com`) does not serve the key today, but the next deploy of `public/` would.

Deleting the files won't help; the key is in git history. It has to be replaced.

## The second door: anyone on your Wi-Fi

- **`http://<this PC>:3104/servex/mcp` answers with no key at all.** I called it through the PC's LAN address and got the full Servex tool list back.
- **Why:** the dev server listens on every interface, and its `/servex/*` proxy forwards LAN callers to Servex from loopback, so Servex's "loopback only" guard passes.
- **The firewall allows it:** the Wi-Fi is set to Public and there is an inbound allow rule for node on that profile.
- **Exposure:** only devices on the same network, not the internet. The proxy's own comment records this as a deliberate choice (2026-09-29) so the phone's assistant keeps working, but it reaches the shell tool, which is probably more than you meant.

## What is working

| Check (no credentials) | Result |
|---|---|
| `monorepo.lew42.com`, any path | 401 Locked |
| `monorepo.lew42.com` WebSocket | 401 |
| `servex.lew42.com`, any path but `/mcp/remote` | 404 |
| `servex.lew42.com/mcp/remote`, no or wrong key | 401 |

- **It is one tunnel, two hostnames**, not two tunnels. Docs: [tunnel.md](Servex/ext/remote/doc/tunnel.md), code in [TunnelNamed.mjs](Server/TunnelNamed.mjs), [Tunnel.mjs](Server/Tunnel.mjs) and [SiteGateway.mjs](Server/SiteGateway.mjs).
- **The socket is not a door from the internet.** A socket that comes through the site gateway may only send `append` and `ping`; `cmd` and `write` are refused ([Socket.js](Server/plugins/SocketServer/Socket.js)). Even with the site key, the site cannot run commands.
- **With the site key you can still** edit pages, drive agents and spend on model calls. That is by design.

## What I'd do next, in order

1. **Rotate the key now.** New `remote.token`, restart Servex and the tunnel gateways, re-paste the connector URL in the Claude app, re-open the site key link on your phone. Cloud voice sessions drop until the re-paste.
2. **Split the keys.** One for the Servex connector, a different one for the site.
3. **Stop secrets reaching the repo.** Have the log writers mask the contents of the `lew42/servex` state files, and add a pre-commit check for them.
4. **Close the Wi-Fi door.** Refuse `/servex/mcp` and the exec/write routes for non-loopback callers in the proxy, keeping the page routes the phone uses.
5. **Put Cloudflare Access in front of both hostnames.** A real login by your email, free, already sketched in tunnel.md. The site key cookie can then go. The Servex connector needs a check of what auth the Claude app supports.
6. **Decide whether the session logs belong in a public repo at all.** They hold your dictations and transcripts.

Steps 1 and 3 matter most; 5 is the proper long-term fix.

## The uncommitted files

I count 52 entries (54 files), not 57. None are code:

| What | Count | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Machine-written ledgers (`usage.jsonl`, `unmerged.json`, `todo.md`, `stale-closes.jsonl`, one voice `session.jsonl`) | 5 modified | Routine churn; commit |
| `feedback-council/` day folders, 11/06 to 11/17 | 7 folders | Agent output the log sweep doesn't cover |
| Briefs, requirements and reviews from spawned masterminds (figma-live, auth-build, auth-merge, youtube-timeline, compaction-forensics) | about 17 | Same; commit |
| YouTube scratch files and folder | 3 | Belong in a scratchpad, not the repo |
| Figma docs in `ext/Figma/doc/` (owner-words, org votes, specs) | 18 | Real docs; commit |
| This session's folder | 1 | Commit |

The tree keeps getting messy because agents write briefs and reviews into session folders that the log sweep doesn't include. Given the above, I would not commit any of it until it has been scanned for the key. My scan found one more working-tree copy of the key beyond the four tracked files; the check that names it was still running when I wrote this.

The background scan finished, and it settles the one loose end from my assessment.

- **The fifth copy of the key is a git-ignored file:** `public/framework/ai/sessions/2026/10/13/cards/session-730e8a7b/page.jsonl`. It is not on GitHub, but it sits under `public/`, so a deploy of that folder could publish it.
- **None of the 54 uncommitted files contain the key.** They are safe to commit on that count. I only checked for this one key, not for other secrets.

Everything else stands: the four tracked files are still public on GitHub and the key still works, so rotating it is still the first step. I have not changed anything and am waiting on your answer about the rotation.

## Where the key lives

Only one of your two places needs updating.

| Place | Uses the key? | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| **Claude Code on this PC** | No. It connects to `http://servex.localhost/mcp`, which only answers this machine and has no key ([.mcp.json](.mcp.json)) | Nothing |
| **Claude app connector** (claude.ai, phone, cloud sessions) | Yes, the key is the end of the connector address | Paste the new address |
| **`monorepo.lew42.com` on your phone** | Yes, same key, stored as a 30-day cookie | Open the new key link once |

## How to change it

The key is one file: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\lew42\servex\remote.token`. Three things read it, each only when it starts.

1. **Move the old key file aside.** Servex writes a fresh random one when it finds none ([RemoteMCP.js:80](Servex/ext/remote/RemoteMCP.js:80)).
2. **Restart Servex.** It now accepts only the new key.
3. **Restart the tunnel** (`node Server/Tunnel.mjs down`, then `up`). This restarts the site gateway with the new key and rewrites `remote.url` and `site.url` in the same folder.
4. **You paste the new address into the Claude app.** Open `remote.url` in Notepad, copy it, and replace the connector's address in the app's connector settings. I can't do this step for you.
5. **You open the link in `site.url` once on your phone.**

I can do steps 1 to 3 and confirm the old key is refused, without the key ever appearing on screen. It takes about a minute, and the app connector is down until you do step 4.

## Keeping it out of the logs this time

- **Copy from the file, never through a chat.** Open `remote.url` yourself and paste it straight into the app. Don't paste it to an agent or ask one to show it. That alone would have prevented this leak.
- **A commit check.** A pre-commit hook that refuses any commit containing the contents of the key files in that folder. It is small, and it catches the mistake whichever way it happens.
- **Mask at the source.** The prompt logger replaces the key with `<key>` before writing a log line.
- **Separate keys.** One for the connector and one for the site, so a leak of one doesn't open both.

The commit check is the one I'd build first, right after the rotation.

One caveat: rotating fixes the key, but your saved chats and dictations are still in a public repo. Making the repo private is a separate decision, and the only thing that covers whatever else is in those logs.

## Your two files

Paste this into the File Explorer address bar to open the folder:

```
C:\Users\mike\AppData\Local\lew42\servex
```

The two files in it:

- **`C:\Users\mike\AppData\Local\lew42\servex\remote.url`**: the new connector address for the Claude app.
- **`C:\Users\mike\AppData\Local\lew42\servex\site.url`**: the new link to open once on your phone.

Neither has a file extension Windows knows, so right-click, choose **Open with**, then **Notepad**.

## What you do

1. **Claude app connector.** Open `remote.url` in Notepad, copy the whole line, and replace the Servex connector's address in the app's connector settings. Until then the app and cloud sessions can't reach Servex.
2. **Phone.** Open the line from `site.url` once in your phone's browser. Your old 30-day sign-in stopped working with the old key.

Copy straight from Notepad into the app. Don't paste either line into a chat, or this key ends up in the logs like the last one.

## Loose ends

- **Old key kept on disk** as `remote.token.old-2026-11-24` in the same folder, so a commit check can scan for it. It is useless now.
- **Running agents** were interrupted by the Servex restart. I did not check which ones were mid-task.
- **Still open:** the commit check, masking in the prompt logger, the Wi-Fi path with no key, and the repo being public.
